title: Topological sort
summary: Order tasks so every dependency comes first, using in-degrees (Kahn's algorithm).
hints: First compute `indeg[v]`: loop over every `u` and every `v` in `g[u]` and do `++indeg[v]`. The vertices with `indeg == 0` have no unmet dependencies; push all of them into a queue.
Repeatedly pop `u`, append it to `order`, and for each neighbour `v` decrement `indeg[v]`. When it reaches 0, `v` is ready: push it.

If the graph has a cycle, the vertices on it never reach in-degree 0, so `order.size() < n` when the queue runs dry. Return an empty vector in that case. `can_finish` is then a one-liner on top of the same idea: build the graph from the pairs (edge `b -> a` for each `{a, b}`) and check whether a full order exists.
